traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests clearly satisfy all acceptance criteria and requirements for docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md.
Key rule implementations: - require-story-annotation rule (src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts) - Tagged with @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md. - Uses DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES imported from helpers/require-story-helpers, and shouldProcessNode for consistent scope/exportPriority handling. - meta: - type: "problem", fixable: "code", hasSuggestions: true. - docs.description and recommended: "error" are set, aligning with ESLint best practices. - schema defines options: { scope: array, exportPriority: enum["all","exported","non-exported"], additionalProperties: false }. - messages.missingStory includes clear, actionable text with function name placeholder and example story path. - create(context): - Reads options[0], falls back to DEFAULT_SCOPE and exportPriority="all". - Builds a local should(node) wrapper around shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority). - Delegates visitor construction to buildVisitors(context, sourceCode, { shouldProcessNode: should, scope, exportPriority }).
- require-req-annotation rule (src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts) - Tagged with @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md. - Imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode from helpers/require-story-helpers and uses checkReqAnnotation from src/utils/annotation-checker.ts. - Options type mirrors story rule: { scope?: DEFAULT_SCOPE[number][], exportPriority?: EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES[number] }. - meta: - type: "problem", fixable: "code". - docs.description and recommended: "error". - messages.missingReq: "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req ..." with explicit example. - schema: same structure as require-story-annotation (scope array of DEFAULT_SCOPE, exportPriority enum of EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES). - create(context): - Normalizes scope: uses DEFAULT_SCOPE when options.scope is missing/empty. - Normalizes exportPriority: default "all". - shouldCheck(node) => shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority). - runCheck(node): if shouldCheck(node) then checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false }). - Returns visitors for: - FunctionDeclaration - FunctionExpression (with early-return when part of MethodDefinition) - MethodDefinition - TSDeclareFunction - TSMethodSignature
Shared helpers and detection logic: - Function detection and scope/exportPriority (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts: - DEFAULT_SCOPE = ["FunctionDeclaration","FunctionExpression","MethodDefinition","TSMethodSignature","TSDeclareFunction"]. - EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - Re-exports DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES from require-story-core. - shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority): - Returns false if node.type not in scope. - isExportedNode walks up the parent chain looking for ExportNamedDeclaration or ExportDefaultDeclaration. - If exportPriority === "exported" -> only exported nodes allowed. - If exportPriority === "non-exported" -> exclude exported nodes. - Otherwise returns true. - require-story-annotation uses buildVisitors (see below) plus shouldProcessNode. - require-req-annotation uses shouldProcessNode in the same way via shouldCheck. - Arrow functions: - buildVisitors defines an ArrowFunctionExpression visitor, but DEFAULT_SCOPE does not include "ArrowFunctionExpression" and schema scope enum only allows the 5 listed types. As a result, shouldProcessNode never returns true for arrow functions in default or any valid config, satisfying "Arrow functions are excluded by default" and preventing them from being enforced for @req.
- Visitor strategy for require-story-annotation (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, REQ-ERROR-LOCATION): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts: - buildFunctionDeclarationVisitor: FunctionDeclaration handler uses shouldProcessNode and helperReportMissing with resolveTargetNode. - buildFunctionExpressionVisitor: FunctionExpression handler uses shouldProcessNode; skips node.parent.type === "MethodDefinition" (so method functions are handled as methods instead of expressions); then uses helperReportMissing. - buildArrowFunctionVisitor: ArrowFunctionExpression handler does the same pattern but is gated by shouldProcessNode, and since scope never includes this type, arrow functions are effectively excluded from enforcement. - buildTSDeclareFunctionVisitor: TSDeclareFunction handler uses helperReportMissing. - buildTSMethodSignatureVisitor: TSMethodSignature handler uses helperReportMissing. - buildMethodDefinitionVisitor: MethodDefinition handler uses helperReportMethod (which anchors error at the method name). - buildVisitors merges all of the above into a single Rule.RuleListener.
- Story annotation detection & error handling (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-ERROR-LOCATION): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node): safely checks sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node) and ensures jsdoc.value is a string containing "@story". - commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node): uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore and scans for "@story" in string values. - leadingCommentsHasStory(node): scans node.leadingComments for "@story". - hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node): tries combination of jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory inside a try/catch to avoid throwing on malformed inputs, satisfying graceful error handling. - resolveTargetNode(sourceCode, node): finds the most appropriate target node for inserting annotations, handling TSMethodSignature (use interface), FunctionExpression and ArrowFunctionExpression in variable declarators, export declarations, and expression statements. - extractName(node): robustly finds a string name from id, key, name, or literal key, walking the parent chain; falls back to "(anonymous)". - reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?): - Checks hasStoryAnnotation first; returns without reporting if already annotated. - Computes functionName via extractName. - Resolves nameNode (id or key Identifier) so the error is anchored at function/method name. - Calls context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingStory", data: { name, functionName: name }, fix: createAddStoryFix(target), suggest: [...] }). - Wrapped in try/catch for robustness. - reportMethod(...) similarly reports at the method key, includes name/functionName, and uses createMethodFix for fix and suggestions.
- Requirement annotation detection and shared parsing for @req (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT): - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts: - Imports FALLBACK_WINDOW and LOOKBACK_LINES from require-story-io to mirror heuristics used for @story. - commentContainsReq: detects if comment value includes "@req" or "@implements". - linesBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node): scans a window of physical lines before the node for @req or @implements, guarded by checks on sourceCode.lines and node.loc. - parentChainHasReq(sourceCode, node): walks parent chain, checks comments via sourceCode.getCommentsBefore and leadingComments for @req/@implements. - fallbackTextBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node): inspects a bounded text window before node.range[0] for @req/@implements; all guarded and wrapped in try/catch to avoid breaking lint. - hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, comments, context?, node?): - If context and node provided, uses linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq to detect annotations. - Falls back to inspecting jsdoc.value and each comment via commentContainsReq. - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts: - Helpers getJsdocComment/getLeadingComments/getCommentsBefore/combineComments unify comment sourcing. - getFixTargetNode: chooses appropriate wrapper for autofix (MethodDefinition, VariableDeclarator, ExpressionStatement), defaulting to node. - createMissingReqFix: inserts "/** @req */\n" before chosen target. - reportMissing(context, node, enableFix = true): - Derives name from getNodeName and anchors node selection at id or key when available. - Builds context.report options with messageId "missingReq" and data { name, functionName: name }. - Attaches fix only when enableFix is true. - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix }?): - Obtains sourceCode, gets jsdoc, leading, comments, combines them, and uses hasReqAnnotation(...). - If !hasReq, calls reportMissing(context, node, enableFix), satisfying REQ-ANNOTATION-REQ-DETECTION and REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT.
Tests demonstrating behavior (all passing in `npm test -- --verbose`): - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - Header references docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED and REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. - Valid cases include: - FunctionDeclaration with JSDoc @story. - FunctionDeclaration with @implements only (accepts as satisfying story requirement). - Line-comment @story above function. - FunctionExpression with inline @story. - Arrow function with @story. - Class method with @story (TypeScript via withTsLanguageOptions). - TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature with @story. - Unannotated arrow function allowed by default (no error), confirming arrow exclusion. - Invalid cases include: - Plain function with no annotations: reports missingStory, suggests adding @story, and autofix output adds JSDoc @story. - FunctionExpression missing @story with expected autofix. - Class method, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature missing @story, with appropriate fix outputs and error data including functionName. - Additional suites cover exportPriority and scope: - `exportPriority: "exported"`: unexported functions without @story are valid; exported functions missing @story are invalid with autofix; exported arrow functions missing @story are ignored, confirming scope/export semantics. - `scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"]`: arrow functions ignored; function declarations missing @story reported.
- tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Header references docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING, plus multi-story support. - Uses runAnnotationCheckerTests to exercise TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature via checkReqAnnotation: - Valid TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature with @req. - Invalid TSDeclareFunction/TSMethodSignature without @req produce missingReq errors. - Main suite `require-req-annotation`: - Valid cases: - FunctionDeclaration with only @req. - Function with only @implements (satisfies requirement coverage). - Function with both @story and @req. - FunctionExpression and MethodDefinition with @req. - TS FunctionExpression in variable declarator, including exported form, with @req. - FunctionExpression ignored when scope only includes FunctionDeclaration. - Export priority behavior: non-exported ignored when exportPriority='exported'; exported required; inverse behavior for 'non-exported'. - Invalid cases: - Missing @req on plain function (no JSDoc), or JSDoc with only @story. - Missing @req on FunctionExpression in variable, anonymous IIFE, MethodDefinition in class/object, TS FunctionExpression (normal and exported). - Scope & exportPriority: confirm that function declarations still reported when in scope; exported and non-exported functions reported appropriately under 'exported'/'non-exported'; methods and function expressions obey exportPriority.
- tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts - Specifically exercises checkReqAnnotation for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature under TypeScript RuleTester configuration. - Confirms autofix: output with "/** @req */" inserted before nodes directly or inside interfaces.
- tests/rules/require-story-helpers.test.ts, require-story-helpers-edgecases.test.ts, require-story-core.test.ts, require-story-core.autofix.test.ts, require-story-core-edgecases.test.ts, tests/rules/require-story-visitors-edgecases.test.ts - Cover edge cases and helper behavior for: - createAddStoryFix, createMethodFix insertion ranges (respecting exports and method bodies). - reportMissing/reportMethod skipping when JSDoc already holds @story, or when preceding lines/comments indicate @story, ensuring graceful error handling. - resolveTargetNode behavior across different parents, including ExportNamedDeclaration, ClassBody, ExpressionStatement. - getNodeName/extractName semantics for various node shapes. - shouldProcessNode returning correct booleans for different node types and exportPriority settings. - jsdocHasStory/commentsBeforeHasStory/leadingCommentsHasStory edge cases where values are not strings. - IO helpers (linesBeforeHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory) detecting annotations in preceding lines, fallback text windows, and parent chains. - buildVisitors returns visitors for FunctionDeclaration and ArrowFunctionExpression and does not throw when nodes lack ids.
- Error message UX & error-location behavior: - require-story-annotation meta.messages.missingStory uses function name placeholder and illustrates the required remediation. - Helpers reportMissing/reportMethod attach context.report at nameNode (id or key), verified by tests in require-story-helpers.test.ts and require-story-core.test.ts. - require-req-annotation’s missingReq message uses data { name, functionName } and checkReqAnnotation’s reportMissing ensures messageId and data are set; tests in require-req-annotation.test.ts assert function names in errors.
Documentation (REQ Documentation acceptance criterion): - docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md - References @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Clearly explains rule purpose, supported node types (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), and that @implements can satisfy story requirement. - Documents options schema: scope and exportPriority, with exact JSON schema and example .eslintrc.js configuration, including defaults and enum values. - Provides correct/incorrect examples, including TypeScript-specific examples.
- docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md - References @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Describes which nodes are validated (function declarations, function expressions, method definitions, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) and explicitly notes that arrow functions are not checked. - States that detection scope matches require-story-annotation’s, satisfying consistent behavior. - Documents `scope` and `exportPriority` with the same semantics and allowed values as require-story-annotation. - Provides clear correct/incorrect examples for JS and TS, including @implements usage for requirement coverage.
Integration and config presets: - src/index.ts (implied by tests) exports rules and configs; plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts verifies: - rules contains both "require-story-annotation" and "require-req-annotation". - configs.recommended and configs.strict include traceability/require-story-annotation and traceability/require-req-annotation with severity "error". - Confirms consistent severity mapping and rule registry.
Test run evidence: - `npm test -- --verbose` output (already executed earlier) shows: - PASS tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - PASS tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - PASS tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts - PASS supporting helper and core tests (require-story-helpers*, require-story-core*, require-story-visitors-edgecases.test.ts). - All 35 test suites passed, 266 tests passed, indicating the implemented behavior aligns with the specified story and its requirements.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS are satisfied. Both require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation enforce their respective annotations over the same function-like constructs using shared/default scope and exportPriority semantics. TypeScript constructs TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature are supported via dedicated visitors and shared annotation-checker utilities. JSDoc and surrounding comments are parsed through a consistent, robust strategy that includes fallback heuristics and graceful error handling. Error messages are clear and actionable, reported at the function or method name. Extensive tests (unit and rule-level) cover core behavior, edge cases, and configuration, and dedicated rule documentation for both rules exists with examples and configuration options. The plugin configuration presets include both rules with appropriate severities. Based on the concrete code and the passing Jest suite, the story is fully implemented.
